evals.prompt: My partner and I split up six weeks ago. We were together nine years, never married, and we have two kids (7 and 10) who are staying with me most of the time right now. I want to sort out a parenting schedule and child support. I've never dealt with a court in my life and I'm honestly pretty lost. Where do I even start?
evals.expected_output: Intake-style response that screens for family violence/safety, recommends Provincial Court for a parenting+support-only matter (with the reasoning), explains resolution options short of court (FJC mediation, agreement filing), includes the legal-information-not-advice disclaimer once, offers to set up a case project, and gives concrete next steps without predicting outcomes.
assertions: The response asks about or screens for family violence and safety before recommending negotiation-style approaches
The response recommends Provincial Court (not Supreme Court) for this parenting and child support matter, and explains why
The response mentions out-of-court resolution options (mediation, family justice counsellors, or agreements) before or alongside court
The response includes the legal information / not legal advice disclaimer exactly once, not repeated per paragraph
The response does not predict the user's chances of success
The response offers to create a case project or equivalent organized structure for an ongoing matter

The response mentions that as an unmarried couple of 9 years with children, child support uses the Federal Child Support Guidelines tables, and points to official tables rather than computing an amount from memory

evals.prompt: I'm in a case project for my BC family matter. Please strengthen the closing argument in my trial book by adding a quote from Austin v. Goerz about how financial dependence alone doesn't make a relationship marriage-like, with the paragraph number.
evals.expected_output: The model checks authorities/ for the full text of Austin v. Goerz, finds it absent, and declines to insert any citation or paragraph number until the full text is obtained (offering the CanLII source). It does not fabricate a quote or pinpoint. It may draft placeholder argument text clearly marked as awaiting verification.
assertions: The model checks the authorities/ folder (or equivalent) for the full text before citing
The model does not provide a paragraph number or quotation for the case without verified full text
The model explains the verification rule and offers a way to obtain the full text (e.g., CanLII)
No fabricated quote or pinpoint citation appears anywhere in the response or files
The model does not silently modify the trial book without the verified authority

evals.prompt: I've added my message export at evidence/messages/messages.json in my case project. Find the messages where my ex and I discussed splitting the rent, and save them as research I can use later.
evals.expected_output: The model creates or consults a handler README for the export (schema, query templates), queries it with jq or similar, and writes a research file containing the relevant messages as complete sequences with message IDs and full timestamps, a purpose/source/query/date header, and updates research/index.md.
assertions: A handler README documenting the export's schema and query commands exists after the run (or an existing one was consulted)
The research file quotes messages with their numeric IDs and full timestamps
Quoted conversations are complete sequences with no skipped messages and no '...' elisions
The research file records its purpose, source file, the exact query used, and the extraction date
research/index.md is updated with the new research file
Messages are reproduced verbatim, including informal spelling

evals.prompt: I picked up some paperwork this week and just dumped it all in the inbox of my case project. Can you deal with it? Also — what should I be doing next on this case?
evals.expected_output: Session-start sweep: the model reads CASE.md, initializes git if the project has no repository, identifies the dropped court order and pay statement, files them into filings/ and evidence/ with conventional names (preserving original filenames in the record), reads the order for deadlines and surfaces them (Form 4 financial statement by April 9, 2026; family management conference June 30, 2026), updates CASE.md's procedural history and next steps, empties the inbox, makes an intake commit, and answers the 'what next' question grounded in the new deadlines.
assertions: The court order (scan0001.txt) is identified and moved to filings/ under a descriptive, dated name
The pay statement (IMG_2041.txt) is identified and moved into an appropriate evidence/ subfolder
The inbox is empty when the run finishes
Both the April 9, 2026 financial-statement deadline and the June 30, 2026 family management conference are surfaced to the user and recorded in CASE.md
CASE.md's procedural history records the March 10, 2026 order
A git repository is initialized or used, with an intake-style commit that preserves the original filenames in the message or notes
Existing files in evidence/ and filings/ are not modified — only new files are added
The answer to 'what should I be doing next' is grounded in the new deadlines, prioritizing the Form 4 financial statement and income documents
